note: What the required CI gates must contain, and what every OTHER workflow in this repository is for. Read from a file so the merge-base ratchet can see it: held as module constants, a job could be excused or a step deleted in the same commit that did it. There are TWO gating workflows since 2026-09-21 -- ci.yml validates the code and pr-policy.yml validates the pull request description -- and `required_commands` below is satisfied by either of them, which is what lets a check MOVE between them without the move reading as a deletion.

not_required.build: it IS the gate; a job cannot require itself

ci.yml.why: the code gate. `build` aggregates every other job here through `needs`, and this is the workflow whose jobs are audited against that list. Its `pull_request` trigger is the DEFAULT set -- opened, synchronize, reopened -- as of 2026-09-22: `edited` came out under #960, because a metadata-only run of this workflow still creates a check SUITE and the ruleset reads the newest suite for an app, so editing a description made build, compile and test read as `expected` again and refused the merge. The retarget that subscription existed for is refused by pr-policy.yml instead. `classify` and the display-name switching on the gated jobs stay and can no longer fire: they are what makes re-subscribing `edited` survivable, because a job skipped under its canonical name publishes `skipped`, which GitHub counts as a satisfied required check.

pr-policy.yml.why: the pull-request BODY check, split out of ci.yml on 2026-09-18 so that editing a description re-runs this and not a macOS test job. `gates_merges` is TRUE as of 2026-09-21, when `pr-policy` was added to the `required_status_checks` rule of ruleset 19060230 beside build, compile and test (integration_id 15368 each, strict left true, bypass_actors left empty) and the ruleset was re-read from the API to confirm the delta was that one added context. The duplicate job in ci.yml came out only after that readback -- removing it first would have deleted the merge block and left a green check that stopped nothing. This field states what the ruleset was observed to hold; no guard in this repository queries the API, and none should on a contributor's run. Since 2026-09-22 it also carries the retarget refusal: it is the only gate subscribed to `edited`, and `--refuse-unvalidated-edit` turns this required context RED for any edit that is not a title or body change, which holds the merge until a push or a reopen puts the code gates over the pull request as it now is.

maintenance.yml.why: roadmap and ADR-index status against GitHub issues. Moved out of `ci.yml` on 2026-09-18: it is bookkeeping about the project rather than a property of the code a pull request changes, and inside the gate a stale row blocked merges that had not touched the roadmap. It still fails; it no longer blocks, and this migration did not move it back.

canon-issue.yml.why: runs on `issues`. There is no merge to block and no `build` job; it comments rather than fails, and that is its whole contract.

release.yml.why: runs on a tag. It gates a RELEASE, not a merge, and its own ordering is what protects that.

publish-mcp.yml.why: publishes registry metadata after a release exists. Nothing about a pull request.

commitlore-preserve.yml.why: runs on `pull_request_target: closed` and only when merged. It preserves records after the fact; there is nothing left to block.
